notes: THE LEDGER GOVERNS THE PRODUCT LAYER, NOT THE LIBRARY — and that is not a
shortcut, it is what a utility-composed library forces.
Every other product in this repository sits on a library with component
class names: `.btn-primary`, `.is-danger`, `.nes-btn`. The verifier reads
`class` attributes, so those vocabularies are governable by construction.
shadcn has no component classes at all. A Button is a string of Tailwind
utilities, and there is nothing stable in the markup for a regex to hold.
So the vocabulary this ledger can enforce is the vocabulary this product
NAMED — the `ids-*` classes in patterns.scss. That turns out to be the
right half to govern: those are exactly the places where iDS diverges from
shadcn, which are the places worth counting. A divergence written as inline
utilities at each call site would be invisible to any check, and nobody
would know how many navy outline buttons the product had grown.
Naming your divergences is what makes them governable. That is the lesson
this example produced, and it is why patterns.scss defines classes instead
of repeating utility strings.
shadcn's own components carry `data-slot` attributes in the markup, which
IS a stable seam — the verifier cannot read attributes today, and that is
a known limit rather than a decision.
ONE MORE LIMIT, found by trying to forbid something. A filled neutral button
is out of pattern here, and the ledger can only refuse it under a NAME —
`ids-btn-neutral`, which this product deliberately does not define. Written
at a call site as the raw utility `bg-neutral`, it escapes the check
entirely. Governing a utility-composed page means naming the things you want
governed; there is no way around that, and it is the same reason the
divergences got class names in the first place.

button.intent: A control that performs an action. The filled primary is shadcn's own Button with `bg-primary`; only the two treatments iDS adds are named here.
button.namespaceNote: Scoped to `ids-btn-`, so it never claims a Tailwind utility. The primary button is deliberately OUT of the ledger: it is unmodified shadcn, and a ledger entry for a pattern the product did not change would be a promise the product is not keeping.

secondary.intent: The supporting action beside a primary one. An outline in the brand's second colour.
secondary.diverges: shadcn's `variant="outline"` draws a neutral line in body text. iDS draws navy, on both the line and the label. That is a ROLE difference rather than a geometry one: the outline reads `border-action` and `fg-action`, which this theme points at the brand's navy while the solid fill stays orange. It is also the reason `border-action` stopped being a hardcoded alias of the fill in layer 2 — Itaú was the first theme that needed to say them separately.
secondary.example: <button data-slot="button" class="ids-btn-secondary inline-flex h-12 items-center justify-center rounded-lg px-6 text-base font-bold">Conhecer os produtos</button>
secondary.notes: Inside `[data-surface="brand"]` it flips to the inverted ink with no extra class — the context does it. That is iDS's `--on-brand` modifier, expressed as a context rather than a variant.

text.intent: The lowest-emphasis action: 'Esqueci minha senha', 'Já sou cliente'. No fill, no line.
text.diverges: shadcn's `variant="ghost"` is neutral and hover-filled. iDS's text button is navy and underlines on hover, which makes it read as a sibling of a link rather than of a button — correct for this brand, where navy IS the interactive ink whether the thing navigates or acts.
text.example: <button data-slot="button" class="ids-btn-text h-9 text-sm font-bold">Esqueci minha senha</button>

neutral.reason: iDS has no filled neutral control. `action_neutral_base` (#3B3B3B) is an INK there — it colours `.ids-icon-button--neutral` and `.ids-action-button--neutral`, both of which are transparent. A solid dark-grey button was invented by the reconstruction and read as out of pattern immediately, which is the useful kind of mistake: the theme still has to DEFINE `neutral` (a theme is a complete set), but this product never fills with it.

field.intent: A labelled text input. The underline field iDS uses everywhere.
field.namespaceNote: `root` is the wrapper only. The BEM parts (`__label`, `__input`, `__message`) are anatomy, not variants — an element carrying one is never itself a field, so it never reaches the pattern check.

default.diverges: shadcn's Input is a bordered box. iDS draws a single bottom rule with a 4px top-corner radius — the filled-field shape. Focus THICKENS the rule to 2px and takes the ring colour, because an underline cannot signal focus by moving a border colour alone: two adjacent greys are not a state change for anyone who cannot separate them.

invalid.intent: A field whose value was rejected.
invalid.diverges: The rule turns `border-danger` and thickens. Carried on the WRAPPER rather than the input so the message text moves with it — the colour and the explanation are one state, and splitting them is how a red border ends up with grey helper text.
invalid.example: Informe os 3 dígitos do operador.
invalid.notes: `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby` are required alongside the class. The class is the appearance; those two are the state.

tabs.intent: Switching between views of the same thing. Used for the access card's 'Agência e conta' / 'CPF' choice.

list.intent: The container, which draws the rule the active tab interrupts.
list.diverges: shadcn's Tabs is a segmented pill on a muted track. iDS underlines.

tab.intent: One tab. The active one is the ONLY place on this page where the selection role is visible as itself.
tab.diverges: The indicator is a 3px underline in `border-selected`. Worth noting what that means in this theme: `selected` and `action` are the same orange, so the underline is the same colour a primary button would be. That is the brand's decision, recorded in theme.scss and warned about by `check-roles()` at build time — not an accident this ledger is papering over.
tab.example: <button role="tab" class="ids-tab text-sm" aria-selected="true">Agência e conta</button>
tab.notes: `aria-selected` drives the appearance, so the accessible state and the visual state cannot drift apart.

pagination.intent: Which page of a carousel is showing.

group.notes: `styled` even though shadcn ships nothing like it. `wrapped` would be the honest state for a component the product built itself — the ledger reserves that word for wrapping a LIBRARY component, and reports the mismatch. Worth knowing the vocabulary has no word for 'ours, from scratch'.

dot.notes: Fills with `fg-default` rather than with a brand colour. Measured on the live site: the chosen dot is white on the brand band and black on a light section, which makes it a CONTEXT decision — the inverted and brand contexts already flip `fg-default`, so it follows for free.

default.diverges: 2px, not a hairline — iDS `size_border_medium`. A class rather than a `border-t-2` utility because the weight is a brand decision, and a utility would scatter it across every call site with nothing to change if it moved.

card.intent: A surface holding one thing. Two interactive states, and they are different roles.
card.namespaceNote: `ids-card-icon` is anatomy — it marks the glyph the hover rule reaches into — so it is inside the namespace but never a root.

interactive.intent: A card that is itself a link or a button.
interactive.diverges: Hover is a NEUTRAL wash, not a brand colour. Read from iDS: `a.ids-card:hover { background: action_neutral_base_soft }`. The icon inside does take the brand ink, which is why the rule reaches one level in. Keeping the surface neutral and the accent local is what stops a grid of cards flashing orange as the pointer crosses it.
interactive.example: …

selected.intent: The chosen card in a set — the recommended product.
selected.diverges: A 2px border in `border-selected`, from iDS `.ids-card.-selected`. This is the one card state that takes the brand colour, and the split is the point: HOVER means the pointer is here, SELECTED means this one is chosen. Painting both with the brand colour would erase the difference — the same discipline this foundation argues for, shipped by a bank.
selected.example: <article data-slot="card" class="ids-card--selected rounded-xl border bg-card p-5" aria-current="true">…</article>
selected.notes: `aria-current` carries the state; the class carries the appearance.

disclosure.intent: A question that opens. The FAQ list.

default.diverges: The rule UNDER a hovered row darkens to `border-color-strong`, which shadcn does not do at all. Worth noting which token: the third step of the line ladder, not a brand colour. A disclosure has no claim to the brand — it is emphasis on a divider, and the ladder exists so that emphasis has somewhere to go that is not the accent.
